messages:
maria: Quick update on the KV-quant bakeoff I ran overnight (FP8 vs INT8 vs baseline fp16). Findings are surprising on long-context tails.

ashok: share numbers?

maria: TL;DR: FP8 KV wins on memory (≈38% drop) but shows a 8–12% increase in p99 latency for 4k+ context. INT8 is middle ground — good memory savings but slightly less p99 regression.

ben: can you paste the perf table and commands?

maria: sure — ran single-GPU perf harness (A100-40GB) with repeated generation to warm KV cache. commands:
```
runtest --model redwood-13b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kv-quant fp16
runtest --model redwood-13b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kv-quant int8
runtest --model redwood-13b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --kv-quant fp8
```

maria: perf summary (mean of 3 runs, same seed):
```
config       mem_kv   p50_ms  p99_ms
fp16 (base)  3.8GB    44ms    118ms
int8         2.6GB    46ms    126ms
fp8          2.3GB    47ms    132ms
```

eva: Hmm p99 jump is concerning. Do we see request-size dependence? short ctx vs long ctx?

maria: yes — for seq<=512, fp8 and int8 p99 ~ baseline (+1–2ms). Above 2k it diverges. Looks like dequant overhead + cache lookup pattern for large KV slices.

ashok: any functional regressions (accuracy)?

maria: ran eval suite (LLM-eval 2k prompts): avg rouge/bleu differences are within noise for both quant schemes. But a small increase in repetition for rare-token next-token on long context for fp8 (~0.6% absolute). Probably quantization noise in KV keys.

ben: hypothesis: FP8 reduces memory but introduces more per-token dequant/quant ops for KV slices leading to jitter in scheduling. Could also be misaligned vectorized kernels.

maria: exactly. Profiling shows hotspots in kv_dequant_kernel (FP8) that cause occasional 1–2ms stalls, which compound at tail.

maria: profiling excerpt:
```
hotspots:
  kv_write: 32% (int8: 28%, fp8: 36%)
  kv_dequant: fp8 22% (int8 10%)
  decoder_attn: 28%
```

eva: ops idea: hybrid approach? keep recent N tokens as fp16 and older KV as fp8/int8. Or quantize on eviction.

ashok: agree. Also try async dequant + prefetch to hide kernel cost.

ben: can we test a simple hybrid: first 512 tokens fp16, rest FP8? If mem savings still decent and p99 recovers, that could be the default for Dedicated.

maria: I'll run a hybrid sweep today (512/1k/2k thresholds) and try async prefetch patch. Will upload artifacts to the bench bucket.

ci-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-benches/kv-quant/1719501234/ (logs + flamegraphs)

eva: thanks — please tag me when you have the hybrid numbers. :thumbsup:
